_intent_notes: #57: what a tool author may put in Result.structured, and what the client receives.
A structured result is a JSON value (MCP 2026-07-28 tools, Structured Content; RFC 8259). Symbols are Ruby's spelling of a JSON string, so symbol keys and values arrive as strings.
Hash and String subclasses (HashWithIndifferentAccess, SafeBuffer) are JSON objects and strings and arrive as plain ones.
Anything else is refused, never as_json'd: a model would publish every column. NaN and Infinity have no JSON form, and JSON text is UTF-8 (RFC 8259 section 8.1).
Keys must be strings or symbols, and two keys that become the same string are a duplicate member (RFC 8259 section 4), refused rather than one silently winning.
A refusal reaches the client as the generic tool error and never echoes the value.
position is where the pair sits: the top-level object, an object nested in an object, or an object inside an array.
